DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE before reading the comments below:
This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
Polyglot: 68 (std-cell utilization about 54 % with four Wire Engines, 64 % with six); global routing has no overflow.
Polyglot: timing-driven global placement. With the DMA added (598k um^2 of cells) the
default (off) left +0.27 ns of setup slack at the slow corner; on: +3.22 ns (P&R, 2026-11-21).
Polyglot: more antenna repair iterations and margin (one violation was left with 3 / 10 %).
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Polyglot: more slew/cap margin in design repair after placement (the SRAM's A_DOUT pins
allow only 0.064 pF and routed wires come out longer than estimated).
Polyglot: wire RC for estimates before routing. The sg13cmos5l LibreLane config leaves
LAYERS_RC empty, so the tech-LEF values are used (Metal2 0.093 fF/um), about half of what
extraction gives on this layout (0.182 fF/um median, 1.52 ohm/um). These are the OpenROAD
RC fit from the sg13g2 config (same Metal1-4 tech-LEF values); TopMetal1 keeps its LEF value.
Polyglot: repair slew/cap again after global routing, with routed-length parasitics.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
Polyglot: 0.05 after placement (polyglot.sdc already keeps 0.1 ns hold uncertainty).
Polyglot: LibreLane's base.sdc with the 0.25 ns clock uncertainty kept for setup only;
hold gets 0.1 ns on top of propagated clocks and the 5 % derate. With base.sdc 4101 of
4402 endpoints 'failed' hold after CTS and repair added 4527 delay buffers (~60k um^2).
Polyglot: area-oriented synthesis. The TT default (DELAY 4) maps to 565k um^2, AREA 0 to
467k (Yosys, four engines); the slow corner still has over 3 ns of setup slack at 50 MHz.
Polyglot: repair setup again after global routing, and keep repairing until 3.3 ns of
slack remain (the slack a 60 MHz clock would need), instead of stopping at zero.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
On-chip SRAM: one IHP 1024x64 macro (8 KB, 784.48 x 336.46 um), bottom right, flipped (FS) so its pins
face the logic above it. The 2048x32 8 KB macro (627 um tall) left too few horizontal tracks:
global-routing overflow 1,463-4,302 in four placements; this shape: 0 (P&R trials, 2026-11-22).
The TT pins are all on the top edge at x = 29..191 um, so the macro sits as far from them as it can.
pdngen stays out of the SRAM's x-range; Polyglot.SramStripes puts full-height trunks there on
the macro's own supply columns (TT needs every stripe full height) and feeds all columns.
A 6 um cell-free ring around the SRAM leaves routing tracks free for nets turning its corner.
Keep signal routing off the macro (CMOS5L routes on Metal2-Metal4 only).
Magic DRC reports illegal overlaps between the tile stripes and the macro's LEF abstract
(Metal4 bar between VDD! and VDDARRAY!); sign off with KLayout DRC on the real GDS instead.
GeneratePDN checks connectivity before Polyglot.SramStripes connects the macro, so its count is
meaningless here. The later IR-drop step reports all VPWR/VGND shapes connected, and LVS is clean.

PDN: pitch/spacing/offset chosen so the Metal4 VPWR/VGND stripes land on the SRAM macro's
supply columns (VDD!/VDDARRAY! at x = 4.26 + 11.24k, VSS! at 9.88 + 11.24k inside the macro,
macro at x = 3.36): every 4th column pair is fed. Values from Ken Pettit's IHP SRAM walkthrough
(https://kdp1965.github.io/ihp-um-janestreet-prism/ihp_sram_macro.html); the default was 50.0.
Custom PDN script: stock LibreLane script without the (empty) macro grid; see pdn_cfg.tcl.
